title: Hotel de Russie vs Bulgari Rome: Courtyard or Scene? (2026) | Suites With Keith
description: Hotel de Russie vs Bulgari Hotel Roma, compared by a travel advisor who visited both in October 2026: courtyard or rooftop, spa or gym, room sizes, atmosphere, and who each one suits.

hero.alt: Hotel de Russie’s large courtyard, with white umbrellas over tables and salmon-pink walls
The Bulgari Hotel Roma rooftop at sunset, a brick walkway under green arches lined with lounge seating

sub: One is built around a big, calm courtyard between Piazza del Popolo and the Spanish Steps. The other is all marble, mosaics and energy, next to the Mausoleum of Augustus. Here is how I would choose.

choose.h3: If you want a garden escape and a pool
choose.lead: A beautiful, large courtyard that feels like an escape from the city, renovated rooms with lemon and orange ceilings, and a spa with an indoor pool.
choose.alt: The indoor pool in the Hotel de Russie spa, tiled in blue mosaic under a starry ceiling

choose.h3: If you want space and a scene
choose.lead: Spectacular. Base rooms the size of junior suites elsewhere, a lively and sophisticated crowd, and more places to eat and drink than I could count.
choose.alt: A Bulgari Hotel Roma base room with a tall upholstered headboard and round brass reading lights

Same rate as booking direct.

band.h2: When you get back from a day on foot, do you want calm or a buzz?
paras: Hotel de Russie is built around its courtyard. It is where everyone gathers, and it feels like an escape from the city around it. Add the spa with an indoor pool and you have somewhere to unwind after the crowds.
The Bulgari is lively, almost like an EDITION but much more sophisticated. The base rooms are very large, and there are so many bars and restaurants that you barely need to leave.
Both put you on busy streets the moment you step out. If you want to come back to a garden and a swim, pick the de Russie. If you want room to spread out and a scene upstairs, pick the Bulgari.

guide.alt: The entry hall of a Bulgari Hotel Roma room, with wood-paneled wardrobes and an oak floor
paras: Space is rare in central Rome, and the Bulgari is one of the exceptions. The base rooms are what other hotels would sell as a deluxe room or a junior suite, so the entry rate already buys real space. I’ll tell you when a higher category is worth it.

At Hotel de Russie, the rooms have been renovated and they are charming, each with a lemon or orange themed ceiling. I also saw a stunning suite with a terrace and fantastic views. Ask me and I’ll tell you which one.

guide.alt: The Bulgari Hotel Roma gym, with racks, benches and plates against warm wood paneling
paras: Hotel de Russie has a nice spa with an indoor pool. That is rare in the centro storico, and a real draw after a day walking the city.
The Bulgari has the biggest gym I saw in Rome: massive, with serious equipment, plus a spa. If you train on vacation, this is the one.

guide.alt: The bar in Hotel de Russie’s courtyard, with arched blue shelves of bottles and a mosaic-fronted marble counter
paras: At the Bulgari, there is a beautiful rooftop bar and pizza restaurant, another bar on the floor below it, and more. Honestly, I’m not even sure how many there are. Downstairs there’s a classic Roman trattoria with fair prices, like €18 pastas. I loved that.
At Hotel de Russie, life happens in the courtyard, with its bar, and in the restaurant with hand-painted walls.

guide.alt: A Hotel de Russie suite terrace looking over Piazza del Popolo’s obelisk to the hills
paras: Hotel de Russie sits between Piazza del Popolo and the Spanish Steps, the golden triangle of Rome on foot. The street out front is busy, so the courtyard is your calm.
The Bulgari is right next to the Mausoleum of Augustus, which is almost done with its renovation. It is on the lively side. If quiet is the priority for either, I would send you to the Eden.

faq.q: Which is better, Hotel de Russie or the Bulgari?
faq.a: It depends on what you want to come home to. Hotel de Russie for the courtyard, the playful renovated rooms and a spa with an indoor pool. The Bulgari for very large base rooms, a lively, sophisticated scene and great dining without leaving the hotel.
The Bulgari. Its base rooms are what other hotels would call deluxe rooms or even junior suites. At Hotel de Russie, ask me about the suite with the views.
For a swim, Hotel de Russie: its spa has an indoor pool, rare in the centro storico. For a workout, the Bulgari, with the biggest gym I saw in Rome plus a spa.

faq.q: Which is better for a first trip to Rome?
faq.a: Hotel de Russie is one I recommend to Rome first-timers: you are between Piazza del Popolo and the Spanish Steps, and you come back to the courtyard.
Not outside the door. At both you step out into busy streets, and the Bulgari is lively inside too. For quiet in the middle of Rome, I pick the Eden or the Corinthia.
